21. CERVICAL CERCLAGE

Definitions:

History indicated Cerclage:

•Cerclage as a result of factors in a women’s obstetric or gyaecological history which the risk of spontaneous 2nd loss or preterm birth.
•Prophylactic cerclage
•Offer @ 11 – 14 weeks.

Ultrasound indicated cerclage:

•Cerclage is inserted as a therapeutic measure in cases of cervical length shortening seen on transvaginal ultrasound.
•Prophylactic length is measured between 14 – 24 weeks by TVS and with an empty bladder
•Done if cervical length is <25m @ gestation <24 weeks.

Emergency cerclage/ Physical exam indicated cerclage:

•Insertion of cerclage as salvage measure in case of premature cervical dilatation with exposed fetal membranes in vagina
•Pt can present with vaginal discharge, bleeding or sensation of pressure
•Can be applied up to 27+6 weeks

Types of Cerclage:

Transvaginal (McDonald):

Suture placed @ cervical isthmus junction without bladder mobilization.

High transvaginal cerclage (Shirodkar)

Purse string suture placed following bladder mobilization, to allow insertion above the level of cardinal ligaments.

Transabdominal Cerclage:

Suture performed via laparotomy or laparoscopy, placing the suture @ cervico isthmic junction.

Occlusion Cerclage:

Occlusion of external OS by placement of a continuous non-absorbable suture.

Purpose is the retention of mucus plug.

Recommendations of Cervical Cerclage:

History indicated

• 3 or more preterm birth or 2nd miscarriages.
•It reduces perinatal death
•No benefit of this cerclage to those who has previous cervical surgery or uterine anomalies
•It is unknown that the characteristics of previous events are helpful or not (painless dilatation, rupture of membranes, prior cervical surgery).

Ultrasound indicated:

•Not affected to those who has incidental short length in late 2nd without risk factors.
•Offered to those who had one or more preterm birth or 2nd loss along with cervical length <25mm measured @ <24weeks.
•Not offered to those who has cervical funneling without short cervical length <25mm
•USG surveillance of cervical length is offered to those who have previous preterm birth or 2nd loss, by TVS with empty bladder and @ 16 – 24weeks, every 2 – 4weeks.
⇨Other women where cervical length need to be measured are either high risk or intermediate risk.

High Risk:

•Previous PPROM < 34 weeks
•Previous use of cerclage
•Known uterine variant
•Intrauterine adhesions
•History of trachelectomy

Intermediate Risk:

•Previous C/S at full dilatation
•LLETZ with excision depth >1cm, more

than 1 procedure or more than 1 cone biopsy.

Multiple Pregnancy:

•not offered either cerclage

 

Raised BMI:

•BMI >25, cerclage is effective in those who has cervical length <25mm

Transabdominal Cervical Cerclage:

•Consider and discuss in women with failed or unsuccessful transvaginal cerclage
•Can be performed pre conceptually or in early pregnancy. Pre conceptually performed cerclage is more effective than antenatal cerclage. It is not associated with subfertility
•Can be performed laparoscopically
•Laparoscopy should be considered where possible as it has fewer complication.
•In case of delayed miscarriage or fetal death, decision of TOP is difficult up to 18 weeks suction curettage or dilatation and curettage can be performed via stitch.
•>18 weeks, stitch can be opened via posterior colpotomy. Failed colpotomy can led to hysterotomy or C/S. decision should be aided by senior obstetrician.

 

 

Emergency Cerclage:

•Individualized decision by taking into account the risks and benefits.
•Women’s decision should be aided by senior obstetrician
•It can prolong pregnancy up to 34 weeks
•It can reduce chance of birth by 2-fold before 34 weeks.
•Advanced dilatation of cervix > 4cm or membrane prolapse beyond external os appears to be associated with higher cerclage failure.
•Not justified beyond 24 weeks due to
•potential risk of iatrogenic membrane rupture and subsequent preterm.

Contraindications of cerclage:

1. active preterm labour

2. clinical Chorioamnionitis

3. continuing vaginal bleeding.

4. PPROM

5. Evidence of fetal defects

6. Lethal fetal defects

7. Fetal death

Risk of cervical cerclage:

•Small risk of intraoperative bladder damage, cervical trauma, membrane rupture, bleeding.
•Cervical trauma/ laceration in case of labour with suture in place.
•High vaginal cerclage needs anaesthesia for insertion and removal.
•No association with PPROM, Chorioamnionitis IOL or C/S (except Emergency cerclage).
•No association with preterm birth or 2nd loss (except emergency cerclage).
⇨Risks and benefits should be discussed with women, both verbal and written information should be given before insertion of cerclage.

Investigation before cerclage insertion:

1. History indicated cerclage.

•1st USG
•Aneuploidy screening

2. USG indicated or emergency cerclage anomaly scan.

3. CRP + TLC count if clinical picture exists.

TLC cut off <14,000/micro liter

CRP cut off <4 mg/dl

4. Amniocentesis

- Not before ultrasound or history indicated cerclage

- Can be done before emergency cerclage in cases where there is clinical suspicion of Intra amniotic infection.

5. Amnioreduction

- No data exists

6. Genital Screening

- Not undertaken routinely

Operative issues:

Can be performed safely as day case procedure

Tocolysis:

•Consider on individual basis
•Not routinely

Antibiotics before cerclage

•Surgeon’s choice

Anaesthesia

•Decision by operating team along with women

Suture material

•Non absorbable suture, surgeon’s discretion.

Type of cerclage:

-Depends on surgeon’s choice
-High/ low cerclage has similar outcome.
•Try to place suture in cervix as high as possible
•No difference between two possible string or single suture. It’s surgeon’s discretion.
•Occlusion suture in addition to primary suture not applied routinely

Bed Rest:

Not recommended routinely

Sexual intercourse:

Abstinence not recommended routinely.

Post cerclage serial USG for cervical length:

-Not done routinely
-Selected USG indicated cerclage cases to offer timely steroid and in utero transfer.

Fetal fibronectin:

•Not recommended routinely
•High negative predictive value can reassure the women.

Progesterone supplementation:

-Not recommended routinely

Arabian pessary or progesterone

-None of them is more effective than cerclage

 

Removal of Cerclage:

1. @ 36+1 – 37weeks before labour

2. Women presenting in active labour, remove cerclage to prevent cervical trauma.

3. Abdominal cerclage need not to be removed. Deliver by C/S and leave cerclage in place.

PPROM and Cerclage removal:

•PPROM between 24 – 34 weeks + No infections => Delayed removal by 48 hours.
•Delayed removal until labour ensures or birth indicated is associated with an risk of maternal/fetal sepsis and is not recommended.
